vignette: Vignette for Mr. Vinay Patel Vinay Patel is a 22-year-old South Eastern Asian male who has been struggling with the aftermath of a traumatic natural disaster that occurred several months ago. Born and raised in Houston, Texas, Vinay now works as a UX Designer at a tech startup. His trauma began on a day like any other until a severe hurricane made landfall, transforming his city into a chaotic landscape. The storm brought torrential rains and winds that destroyed homes and left many injured or displaced. Vinay was at work when the disaster struck. He recalled feeling overwhelmed by the chaos outside his office window—trees uprooted, power lines down, and water flooding streets in mere minutes. Despite efforts to evacuate orderly, panic set in as people rushed to get to higher ground. Vinay found himself caught in a surge of panic-stricken individuals, jostling for space on a stairway that became dangerously crowded. In the midst of this chaos, he fell and hit his head, leaving him with lingering neck pain. Since the disaster, Vinay has been plagued by vivid triggers. The persistent neck pain often brings back the memory of falling and the fear he felt in those moments. Even more unsettling are the times when he feels physically unwell—a sensation that transports him back to the nausea-inducing fear during the storm's peak. These sensations make him acutely aware of his body, as if it is constantly signaling danger. Vinay’s memories of the event have taken on a surreal quality. At times, the memory seems so extreme and unbelievable that he questions whether it truly happened to him. During moments when the trauma resurfaces, he can vividly taste the metal-like flavor from the air during the storm. He also experiences intense emotions without any clear image or context, leaving him feeling overwhelmed by a sense of loss and fear. These triggers have deeply affected Vinay’s daily life as a UX Designer. Working in an open office space means constant exposure to potential stressors, such as sudden loud noises that can mimic the sounds of the storm. He has started avoiding certain areas of his workplace where he feels particularly vulnerable, leading to increased isolation from colleagues and decreased productivity. Vinay's distrust of others has grown significantly since the event. He finds it difficult to trust even close friends and colleagues, believing that people are not what they seem. This suspicion has led him to withdraw socially, feeling more isolated and disconnected from those around him. The sense of not belonging anywhere—neither at work nor among his peers—has compounded his feelings of isolation. Vinay’s relationship with his family has also been strained. He avoids talking about the disaster, preferring silence over recounting the traumatic events. This withdrawal has led to misunderstandings and a growing distance between him and his loved ones. What finally brought Vinay to seek help was the realization that his symptoms were becoming too overwhelming to manage on his own. He feared that he might lose his job due to decreased performance and felt increasingly hopeless about ever feeling normal again. Despite these fears, there is also a flicker of hope within him—that with support and guidance, he can regain control over his life and find a way to reintegrate into the world without constant dread. In therapy, Vinay hopes to understand why his body and mind continue to relive that harrowing day. He wants to learn how to manage his triggers better and rebuild trust in others so he can feel connected again. His journey towards healing will require navigating through these complex emotions and memories, but he is determined to find a path forward.
